observations: The certified operator-leaf and connected single-transformer-layer gates passed. The hash-validated lower-layer certificates remain reusable, and no current board trace explicitly contradicts a named leaf or connected-kernel invariant. The certified kernel remains an elastic variable-latency token pipeline: boundary order and cross-token overlap are preserved requirements, not strict same-cycle stage completion.

The current board-layer direct failure is static/runtime-harness binding, not an RTL functional failure. case_axi_ddr_interface reports unbound source identity, Vivado compile authority, command authority references, and simulator executable. functional_sim was dependency-blocked because board_testbench_artifact_loading lacks exact_sample_top_module; the missing semantic-evidence report is downstream of those skipped gates.

The prior VCS diagnosis is historical-only because its evidence binding is not current. The previous nonterminal live trace and prior repair feedback may guide evidence collection, but cannot justify a hardware root cause. It must be replaced by current hash-bound termination provenance and, if authorized, a terminal replay.

Prior repair execution specifically requires the raw simulator termination marker/log tail, current remote runner wall-time and cycle budget, and authorization to replay the unchanged hash-bound 24-layer board closure through a terminal event. Until then, a frontier stall or missing post-output reports cannot be classified as connected-kernel liveness, AXI, DDR, or wrapper RTL failure.

sacg_memory_truth has 15 active same-scope contamination barriers, including current barriers contamination_barrier.0348 through contamination_barrier.0352. They make the rejected Stage7/Stage8 artifacts planning and debug evidence only, not validated inputs. Open retry requests retry_request.0136, retry_request.0140, retry_request.0141, retry_request.0142, retry_request.0143, and retry_request.0144 require bounded repair followed by a fresh Stage7 result; no open same-scope backtrack request exists.

No retry-reconciliation contract was supplied. The active barriers and retries must therefore remain active until a fresh checker-governed Stage7 result is produced; this repair decision does not clear or promote any rejected artifact.

The renewed board contract and replay must preserve the same immutable target checkpoint, complete Transformer-block tensor catalog, deterministic or real input provenance, independent target-model expected outputs, complete DUT weight-consumption binding, data order and shape contracts, memory/runtime mapping, exact wrapper/source hashes, and frozen numeric comparison policy. Embedding/tokenization, final norm, LM head/logits, and sampling remain outside the DUT and its board golden boundary.
proposed_actions: Re-discover and bind the exact user-supplied board project and Vivado export facts into the board testbench identity and canonical VCS compile plan; use the discovered top-module fact rather than a hardcoded substitute, then rerun the failed AXI/DDR interface gate.

After the binding gate passes, collect current hash-bound remote VCS termination provenance. This is a verification-capability repair, not a hardware repair, and must distinguish a remote execution-budget stop from a simulator terminal event.

Obtain bounded authorization for any replay exceeding the current remote budget, then run the unchanged exact board closure to a terminal event with the immutable semantic contract and required board-level check sequence.

Only if a completed current trace fails, localize its earliest board causal boundary and request a targeted board replay. Keep lower layers closed unless the localization directly contradicts a named certified invariant; otherwise repair only the identified current-layer harness, integration, wrapper, runtime, or instrumentation slice.
risks: Guessing a top module, simulator executable, Vivado export context, wrapper path, or source hash would violate the exact sample-project requirement and could silently substitute a simplified board shell.

Changing generated expected outputs, checkpoint, stimulus, loader scope, numeric tolerance, or comparison policy to obtain a passing replay is prohibited. A terminal replay must use independent target-model outputs for the same immutable Transformer-block inputs and checkpoint.

The prior nonterminal run may reflect remote budget termination or simulator-side failure. Treating it as a hardware deadlock, or modifying RTL/report writers to fabricate downstream reports before terminal evidence exists, would be an unsupported causal repair.

A board output/lifecycle frontier symptom alone cannot reopen the connected kernel. Lower-layer revalidation requires a current hash-bound trace containing direct core start, ingress, egress, a named causal boundary contradiction, and the relevant current certificate evidence.

Backend synthesis, implementation, bitstream generation, runtime-ABI release, and board runtime are later-stage actions and remain blocked until every required current board-layer gate and semantic-evidence check passes.

constraints: exact user-supplied board wrapper and source-hash requirement
